q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of an industrial gearbox?
title: Gearbox carbon footprint per unit
short: Weigh the cast housing, steel gears and shafts, bearings and oil per gearbox and multiply by supplier figures. Add machining, gear cutting, heat treatment and assembly energy, then divide the plant's energy by gearboxes built.

ul: Gear hobbing, heat treatment and grinding.

p: Report per gearbox by type and weight. A large gearbox can weigh many times a small one, so weight-based allocation of plant energy is usually fairer than a plain count.

example.title: Worked example: plant energy per unit (one month)
lines: Plant total: 116,750 / 2,000 = 58.4 kg CO2 per unit
Add housing, gears, bearings and oil for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
